title: Prechecks: improve messaging + remediation hints; add --json report output for Support
author: Devon Price
description: Context: During the beta upgrade rehearsals and a recent Support escalation (SUP-1842), precheck failures were correct but hard to interpret (generic messages, missing remediation, and inconsistent exit reasons). This PR tightens the precheck UX and adds a machine-readable `--json` output mode so Support/PS can ingest reports and quickly route issues (permissions vs capacity vs version skew) without asking customers to copy/paste console output. Changes: (1) Precheck messaging: standardize formatting across checks and include check_id, component, severity, failing predicate, and a remediation block with actionable steps (commands/links) and “why this matters” context; (2) Remediation hints: add targeted guidance for the most common beta failures (storage class detection, snapshot/IAM permissions, disk space, Kubernetes version); (3) JSON report output: `redwood-private-installer precheck run --json` prints a stable schema (versioned) to stdout; it includes summary counts, per-check results, timestamps, and a correlation id; (4) Redaction: avoid leaking secrets (we do not serialize env vars, kubeconfig contents, or token values; kube context name is included but namespaces and resource names are truncated when coming from error strings); (5) Support-friendly exit codes: preserve existing exit code behavior for human runs, but explicitly map JSON `summary.overall_status` to exit code for automation. Notes: Default human output remains unchanged aside from improved text; `--json` disables ANSI coloring and suppresses interactive “retry” prompts (still returns non-zero appropriately). The JSON schema is intended for ingestion into diagnostics bundles and future support tooling; see examples below. Example JSON (truncated): `{ "schema_version": "1.0", "correlation_id": "upg-01HPK...", "overall_status": "fail", "checks": [{"check_id":"k8s.version","severity":"error","status":"fail","message":"Kubernetes version 1.23 is below minimum 1.25","remediation":["Upgrade cluster control plane to >=1.25","See docs: https://docs.redwood.inference/private/prereqs#kubernetes"],"evidence":{"detected_version":"1.23"}}] }`
commits: prechecks: standardize failure formatting + remediation block
cli: add --json output mode for precheck run
prechecks: add remediation hints for storage class + snapshot permissions
tests: golden tests for json schema + message snapshots
docs: update help text + examples for Support
conversation: Rafael Mendes (review): The remediation hints read much better. One concern: Support will paste JSON into tickets; can we ensure error strings don’t contain full resource names/paths that might be sensitive? Also, should `--json` include installer version + git sha for correlation with release trains?

Devon Price (author): Good call. I added a small sanitizer for evidence/error fields that strips full filesystem paths and truncates Kubernetes resource names when they come from raw errors. Also added `installer.version` and `installer.build_sha` to the JSON root (pulled from existing version info). Pushed commit: `cli: include version/build_sha in json report + sanitize evidence`.

Sean Gallagher (review): From SRE side: can we get a stable `correlation_id` that matches the upgrade correlation id we’re using elsewhere? At least for prechecks, generate one that Support can reference in Slack/incident-bot threads.

Devon Price (author): Yep. If `--correlation-id` is provided we use it; otherwise we generate `precheck-<ulid>` and print it both in human and JSON outputs. In the future upgrade runs can pass the upgrade correlation id through to prechecks. Added to help text + tests.

Dev Patel (review): JSON schema needs to be versioned and explicit about what is “stable”. Please add `schema_version` and avoid breaking changes without bumping. Also: can we keep the output deterministic (ordering) for diffing in tickets?

Devon Price (author): Added `schema_version: 1.0` and pinned ordering by sorting checks by `check_id` before rendering. Also ensured `remediation` is always present (may be empty) so downstream parsers don’t need null checks. Added golden tests for deterministic output.
Kenji Nakamura (review): Minor UX: in human output, the remediation block header should be short and scannable. The previous beta feedback was “too much text”. Maybe: `Fix:` and `Why:` lines.
Devon Price (author): Updated formatting: `Fix:` bullet list + optional `Why this matters:` one-liner. Kept longer context behind `--verbose` (unchanged).

Jacob Stein (review): For diagnostics bundles, can we write the JSON report to a known filename when collecting? Looks like you added a collector hook—please confirm it won’t overwrite existing bundles without warning.

Devon Price (author): The diagnostics collector writes `precheck-report.json` into the bundle directory for that run; bundle root already uses a unique timestamped folder. No overwrite risk unless user manually reuses the same folder, which the tool currently disallows.
Rafael Mendes (approve): Approving. This will save us time on escalations. Please add a note to the runbook next sprint to prefer `--json` in customer repros.
Sean Gallagher (approve): LGTM. Thanks for keeping default output intact and gating JSON behind a flag.
Dev Patel (approve): Approved with schema_version + deterministic ordering. Please keep schema additions backwards compatible within 1.x.
release_notes: Private installer: precheck failures now include clearer remediation hints and standardized formatting.
Private installer: `precheck run --json` outputs a versioned, machine-readable report for Support ingestion and diagnostics bundles.
